NEXTGEN COMMERCE · THAILAND · GLOBAL COLLABORATION

Website NextGen

Connecting local user needs with a shared global commerce experience.

UX/UI designGlobal & local teamsDesktop & mobile

01 / CONTEXT

A global platform. A local experience.

NextGen Commerce brought together shopping, promotions, subscriptions, registration and post-purchase journeys, with Thailand as the pilot market. I collaborated with the global team and Thailand stakeholders on UX/UI design, reusable components, research activities, usability testing and UAT.

02 / UNDERSTAND

Start with people and their tasks.

Research activities included workshops, internal sessions and in-depth interviews, followed by usability testing of purchase, A Point, order and account journeys. Further testing focused on SOP Manual in the cart. Staff and Amway Business Owners (ABOs) helped the team examine the experience in a local context. Across the user-testing programme, 40 users participated in rounds organised into groups of 8. The June 2024 co-creation report below documents one 8-person round.

User research

Explore user needs, existing journeys and local expectations through workshops and interviews.

Define the problem

Review friction around promotions, coupon visibility, delivery fees, cart controls and payment or order states.

Feedback from UAT and trial use by staff and Amway Business Owners (ABOs) was grouped by category and journey to make recurring issues visible to the team. This summary is a separate evidence set from the June 2024 co-creation study.

RESEARCH EVIDENCE / THAILAND CO-CREATION

From participant observations
to design recommendations.

As part of a wider testing programme involving 40 users in groups of 8, the June 2024 co-creation study examined how participants navigated subscription purchasing, promotions and registration. The findings gave the Thailand and global teams specific interaction problems to review together.

8Participants in this June co-creation round
2Key tasks explored
4–5 Jun 2024Study dates

My contribution

I prepared prototypes and test tasks, co-facilitated the sessions and documented participant observations. I collaborated with the team to analyse findings and recommend improvements, then translated the findings into UI refinements and coordinated the proposed changes with the global team.

TASK 1

SOP proxy order + PWP promotion

Create a subscription order for a downline, then navigate the purchase-with-purchase promotion journey.

TASK 2

New ABO purchase with registration

Explore sponsoring, purchasing and registration, including identity verification and confirmation.

Three findings that informed the design work

01 / CART NAVIGATION

A clear route back to shopping

What we observed

Participants could not easily find how to leave the cart and add more products. Some expected an “Add More Products” action.

Design recommendation

Make the route to continued shopping visible. The report recommends adding bottom navigation.

View study evidence

02 / PROMOTION DISCOVERABILITY

Put special-price products where people look

What we observed

Participants overlooked the special-price product selection at the top of the cart and suggested a lower position.

Design recommendation

Review promotion placement near the coupon section at the bottom of the screen, as recommended in the study.

View study evidence

03 / IDENTITY VERIFICATION

Make the verification action understandable

What we observed

The registration findings included uncertainty about the Verify link and why identity checking was required.

Design recommendation

Give verification a more prominent button and explain the purpose of the identity check with visible supporting text.

View study evidence

What the study contributed

The study documented concrete friction points and recommendations for design review. My role connected prototype preparation, observation, synthesis and UI refinement with the global team.

04 / DESIGN & PROTOTYPE

Build clarity into screens and components.

Work with the global team to translate local requirements into screen structure, interaction states and reusable components. Use prototypes and reviews to connect global consistency with Thai content and commerce rules.

The selected designs show Homepage, Product Category, Promotion, SOP, About Amway and Registration / ABO / Member views, with product cards, campaign tiles and mobile navigation.

FLOW COMPARISON / GLOBAL DESIGN COLLABORATION

Help familiar journeys work in NextGen.

I compared the existing Amway Thailand website with the NextGen experience that would replace it. The goal was to identify extra steps, unclear actions and changes that could disrupt users familiar with the existing system.

I created side-by-side flow comparisons and annotated recommendations, then worked with the global design team to refine NextGen interactions for the Thailand market. The comparisons helped make local user expectations and specific improvement opportunities concrete during design reviews.

SOP subscription: preserve a familiar journey

The comparison maps the existing self-subscription journey at 3 pages / 7 clicks and the NextGen beta journey at 6 pages / 10 clicks. I highlighted the unclear entry point, extra confirmations and missing benefit information for review with the global design team.

Promotion purchase: make eligibility easier to follow

The existing flow added two qualifying products in one action. The NextGen beta flow added one at a time and made the product-selection control less visible. I compared these behaviours and recommended clearer selection cues and quantity handling.

Cart: connect feedback with UI changes

I annotated cart search, delete-all controls, SOP card length and promotion placement. The recommendations bring together co-creation and Beta feedback to make cart contents and available actions easier to understand.

Pickup: make selection and confirmation visible

I proposed clearer delivery and pickup controls, selecting a shop directly from the map, a visible map action and carrying the selected shop back into the flow without an unnecessary confirmation.

“Current Website” in these historical artifacts means the Thailand website in use at the time of comparison; “NGC” means the NextGen beta experience. Page and click counts describe mapped flows, not measured completion times or verified post-release improvement.

05 / TEST & ITERATE

Bring staff and ABO feedback into the design.

Participate in usability testing of key journeys with staff and ABOs, review task completion and areas of confusion, and feed findings into design reviews with global and local stakeholders. Refine screens, interaction states and language, then support handoff and UAT.

Understand whether people can follow and complete the intended journey.

BETA FEEDBACK / DOCUMENTED IMPLEMENTATION

Follow recommendations through to delivery.

The improvement report dated 16 May 2025 records completed changes alongside planned work. It adds implementation evidence to the earlier co-creation findings and Beta 2 recommendations.

Restore a route out of the cart

The co-creation study identified difficulty returning to shopping. The improvement report records cart navigation as fixed on 11 March 2025 and shows the navigation in the cart.

Make cart contents and actions visible

The same report records visible bundle child items and a delete-all-cart action as fixed on 11 March 2025. The Thai-vowel input defect is recorded as fixed on 20 January 2025.

Completion dates are reported in the supplied improvement document. They establish documented implementation status, not an independently verified retest or measured usability uplift. Other entries in the report carry planned dates and are not presented here as completed.

Research scope: the 40-user programme organised in groups of 8 is separate from the Beta rollout populations listed in this report. These participation figures are not combined.

From research to delivery.
